chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) concerning

A man married a woman based on her stipulation or based on his stipulation, and he died or she died before he consummated the marriage with her, then he said to her: provision (mut'ah), inheritance, and no dowry for her.

He said: If he divorces her and had married her based on her stipulation, the stipulation does not exceed five hundred silver dirhams, which is the dowry of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.المُتْعَةُ: Provision given to the wife upon divorce or death before consummation
key_terms.مُهُورِ نِسَاءِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The dowry of the wives of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights of a wife if the husband dies or divorces her before consummating the marriage according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the distinction between 'mut'ah' (provision) and inheritance in cases of pre-consummation dissolution, emphasizing that death triggers full inheritance rights without deducting the dowry. In contrast, divorce imposes a cap on the dowry at five hundred dirhams, aligning with the customary mahr of the Prophet's wives, a ruling significant in Shia jurisprudence for determining financial settlements in khula or talaq scenarios. The narration underscores the practical application of Quranic principles regarding equitable treatment of women in marital contracts.
